subject: Compiler directives
notes: kb/Work PB1365 (wave 1019 B). Both halves hold on a fresh build. (a) program-text area: a directive at column 8 with sequence-area content (cols 1-6) is read, a directive at column 7 is COBOL2616 (conformance:cases/7.3-Compiler-directives/pb1365_turn_directive_in_program_text_area; unit:ReferenceFormatLogicalConversionTests.FixedFormDirective_IsRecognizedInTheProgramTextArea; SR-7.3.3-2). (b) 'followed only by space characters and an optional inline comment': the one parse strips the inline comment quote-aware, the closed-word directives reject a trailing word through CheckOperand (COBOL1911: LISTING, PROPAGATE, REF-MOD-ZERO-LENGTH, LEAP-SECOND, CALL-CONVENTION, PUSH, POP, SOURCE FORMAT), ELSE / END-IF / END-EVALUATE reject any operand (PB806), and EVERY directive word of EVERY stage-owned row (TURN COBOL0718, FLAG-02/-14 COBOL1622, COBOL-WORDS COBOL1623, DEFINE/IF/EVALUATE/WHEN/DISPLAY COBOL1619) rejects a word after its conforming operand in fixed and free form and accepts its operand with an inline comment: StageOwnedDirectiveOperandDriftTests derives the word set from the Stage rows, so a new stage-owned directive without a witness line is a red test. The PB1365 hole was TURN's loop breaking at CHECKING. retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Editions/CompilerDirectiveLine.cs#StripInlineComment (kb/Work PB2621: the directive line's inline comment is found by the one literal reader, CobolSourceText.InlineCommentAt, which CompilerDirectiveLine.TryParse asks)
